skill.name: json-canvas
skill.description: Create and edit JSON Canvas files with valid nodes, edges, groups, colors, and Obsidian-compatible canvas structure.
skill.summary: Build valid JSON Canvas files for Obsidian mind maps, flowcharts, project boards, and visual notes.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JSON examples, ordinary documentation terms, and reference URLs. I found no executable code, shell invocation, network request logic, data exfiltration intent, or prompt injection attempt in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: This skill enables skills-compatible agents to create and edit valid JSON Canvas files (`.canvas`) u
JSON Canvas is an open file format for infinite canvas data. Canvas files use the `.canvas` extensio
- `edges` (optional): Array of edge objects connecting nodes
| `id` | Yes | string | Unique identifier for the node |
| `x` | Yes | integer | X position in pixels |
| `y` | Yes | integer | Y position in pixels |
| `color` | No | canvasColor | Node color (see Color section) |
| `text` | Yes | string | Plain text with Markdown syntax |
| `file` | Yes | string | Path to file within the system |
| `subpath` | No | string | Link to heading or block (starts with `#`) |
| `label` | No | string | Text label for the group |
| `background` | No | string | Path to background image |
| `cover` | Fills entire width and height of node |
| `ratio` | Maintains aspect ratio of background image |
| `repeat` | Repeats image as pattern in both directions |
| `id` | Yes | string | - | Unique identifier for the edge |
| `fromNode` | Yes | string | - | Node ID where connection starts |
| `fromSide` | No | string | - | Side where edge starts |
| `fromEnd` | No | string | `none` | Shape at edge start |
| `toNode` | Yes | string | - | Node ID where connection ends |
| `toSide` | No | string | - | Side where edge ends |
| `toEnd` | No | string | `arrow` | Shape at edge end |
| `label` | No | string | - | Text label for the edge |
The `canvasColor` type can be specified in two ways:
1. All `id` values must be unique across nodes and edges
2. `fromNode` and `toNode` must reference existing node IDs
8. Color presets must be `"1"` through `"6"` or valid hex color

content.value_statement: Creating Obsidian canvas files by hand can cause invalid nodes, edges, and layout data. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce valid JSON Canvas structures.
actual_capabilities: Create .canvas files with text, file, link, and group nodes.
Define edges with sides, endpoints, labels, and colors.
Use documented JSON Canvas color presets and hex colors.
Plan readable layouts with coordinates, sizing, and spacing.
Build examples for mind maps, project boards, research maps, and flowcharts.
Check required fields and node references against the documented rules.
limitations: Does not render a visual canvas preview.
Does not run external validation tools by itself.
Does not create image or attachment files referenced by file nodes.
Covers the fields documented in this skill and JSON Canvas Spec 1.0.

use_cases.title: Map Research Sources
use_cases.description: Create a canvas that connects papers, notes, links, and central research questions.

use_cases.title: Plan Project Boards
use_cases.description: Build grouped boards with task cards, status lanes, and clear visual spacing.

use_cases.title: Draft Knowledge Maps
use_cases.description: Turn outlines into connected visual notes for Obsidian or another JSON Canvas viewer.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Mind Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple JSON Canvas mind map for this topic. Use one central text node, three supporting text nodes, and labeled edges.

prompt_templates.title: Organized Project Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian .canvas project board with To Do, In Progress, and Done groups. Add task nodes with readable spacing.

prompt_templates.title: Research Canvas With Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a research canvas from these notes. Include text nodes, file nodes, link nodes, and edges that explain each relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Validate And Improve Canvas
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this .canvas structure for missing fields, invalid references, poor spacing, and unclear labels. Return a corrected version and explain changes.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a mind map about a product launch plan.
output: A central launch plan node with supporting strategy, timeline, risks, and metrics nodes.
Edges connect each support node to the central topic with clear labels.
The layout uses consistent spacing and valid canvas node dimensions.

output_examples.input: A user wants a research canvas for notes, papers, and links.
output: A research question node anchors the canvas.
File and link nodes represent source material without creating those files.
Labeled edges show which sources support, challenge, or illustrate the topic.

output_examples.input: A user provides a broken canvas with missing edge targets.
output: A validation review identifies missing node references and unsupported field values.
The corrected canvas keeps the original intent while using valid node and edge rules.

best_practices: Use unique 16-character IDs for every node and edge.
Keep node spacing consistent so the canvas stays readable.
Check every edge endpoint against an existing node ID.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse node IDs across different items.
Do not point file nodes to attachments that do not exist.
Do not crowd many nodes into the same coordinates.

faq.question: What is JSON Canvas?
faq.answer: JSON Canvas is an open format for infinite canvas data used by Obsidian and related tools.

faq.question: Can this skill create Obsidian .canvas files?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the agent to create valid .canvas structures with nodes, edges, groups, and layout data.

faq.question: Does this skill render the canvas visually?
faq.answer: No. It creates or reviews the canvas data, but a compatible app must render the visual view.

faq.question: Can it include files and links?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents file nodes and link nodes, including paths, subpaths, and external URLs.

faq.question: Can it repair an existing canvas?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review required fields, node references, allowed values, and layout clarity.

faq.question: Does it run commands or access the network?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation only. It contains examples and reference links, not executable tooling.
